name: Pepys
summary: Audio and video transcription with timestamps in 99 languages, summaries and exports; pay per hour of audio with no subscription.
best_for: researchers, journalists, podcasters and students who transcribe audio or video in bursts and want to pay per hour, with no monthly subscription
skip_if: you need live meeting capture with a bot in the call, you transcribe every day and prefer a flat monthly plan, or you want a tool we have tested on real recordings
honest_knock: Speaker labels use three times the credits. The team plan has no visible price. The page shows euros but bills in USD, and all sales are final. Pepys Dictate, the Mac dictation app, is a separate product. Word-level timing exports (JSON, SRT, VTT) come from transcripts made from audio; the founder wrote to us on 20 November 2026 that sources built only from existing captions may not contain that timing data. We did not test word-level export.

pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-13 on pepys.co/pricing, amounts shown in euros and billed in USD) Pepys has a free account and pay-as-you-go credits. The free account gives 60 minutes once, with no card, files up to 1 GB, transcription in 99 languages with timestamps, AI summary, chapters and chat, translation, exports to TXT, DOCX, PDF, SRT, VTT and JSON, and API access metered on your free minutes. Paid credits cost €1.1 an hour on purchases under €17.6, €0.88 an hour from €17.6 and €0.75 an hour from €74.8. The smallest pack shown is 10 hours for €11 and the buy button offers 20 hours for €17.6. Any purchase gives you files up to 5 GB and 10 hours, unlimited Google Drive, OneDrive and Zoom imports, batch upload of up to 100 files, speaker labels at 3 credits per minute, word-level timestamp exports and removal of the Pepys mark. The page says credits never expire, personal use has no subscription and all sales are final. Teams can add a flat monthly plan. We did not buy credits, so we do not know the tax added. Re-read on 15 November 2026 with a plain fetch of pepys.co/pricing: the hourly rates (€1.1, €0.88 and €0.75) are unchanged, and the page now lists packs of 10 hours for €11, 30 for €26.4, 50 for €44, 75 for €66, 100 for €74.8 and 200 for €149.6, plus a custom top-up from $5. It also prices the team plans: Starter €16.72 a month for 20 shared hours, Team €43.12 for 60 and Scale €87.12 for 140, with no per-seat fee and unused hours kept. The terms say prices exclude tax, which Polar, the merchant of record, adds at checkout.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 19 November 2026 the session tested Pepys on the free account with 60 minutes and no card. A 53-second test recording came back in under 20 seconds with 2 word errors in 135 words, and the speaker pass fixed both for 1 extra credit. The app prices hour packs in US dollars while the pricing page shows euros. Account and start: we created the free account, which gives 60 minutes with no card. Our AI assistant ran the test in its own tab on 19 November 2026 from 12:40 CET; the interface was in English. The sidebar showed Credits 1 h. New transcription accepts uploads, Google Drive, OneDrive and Zoom, and pasted links; Free includes 3 connected-source imports, one recording at a time. Core action, a recording to a transcript: a 53-second English test recording with a reference text of 140 words. The first upload as .m4a was refused with Only audio or video files can be transcribed., because our upload tool sent no file type; the same recording as .wav went through. Upload to transcript took well under 20 seconds: 0:53 · 1 min billed · 135 words · 1 speaker · ENGLISH. The transcript had 2 word errors in 135 words (fogs for fox, wake for week), about 1.5 per 100 words. AI notes came with it at no extra cost, and one key point itself flagged second wake as a likely transcription error. Speakers: Detect speakers started a new pass at once, with no cost warning first, and finished in about 30 s: 136 words · 1 speaker, with both errors gone. The recording has one voice, so several speakers were not tested. Export: SRT, VTT, TXT, Markdown, DOCX, PDF, JSON and NVivo, with speaker labels and timestamps as options, and word-level cues. One TXT export was read; its last line was Transcribed with Pepys, the brand mark on free exports. The file was deleted afterwards. Credits: BALANCE 58 minutes · 58 credits · 1 credit = 1 minute · never expire, so the transcript used 1 credit and the speaker pass 1 more. Plans: in the app, in US dollars, 10 hours $12.50 ($1.25/hr), 20 hours $20, up to 200 hours $170 ($0.85/hr). The pricing page shows euros billed in USD, 10 h EUR 11 to 200 h EUR 149.6, and says Uploaded recordings are removed after about 30 days and All sales final. Team plans start From $19/month. Checkout, seen up to paying: Buy on 10 hours opened a Polar checkout for Pepys - Transcription Credits at US$ 12,50 with a saved payment method; nothing was clicked or filled in, and no screenshot was kept because it showed payment details. Cancelling: there is no subscription. Delete account sits under Settings, Account; it Permanently removes your recordings, transcripts, derived files, API access and account profile. Not clicked. Files are stored in the European Union. Not tested: several speakers, batch upload, Zoom or Drive imports, the API, a paid purchase, translation and long files. Clean up: the account and one transcript stay, with 58 minutes left; the TXT export was deleted. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: Detect speakers starts at once with no cost warning. Free exports carry a Pepys line. The pricing page shows euros while the app and checkout show US dollars.
